stories.title: Russell Westbrook Retires From NBA — NEW

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Russell Westbrook is retiring from the NBA.

209 career triple-doubles.
9x All-Star. 2017 MVP.
18 seasons.

The most statistically unique player who ever played the game.

#NBA

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Westbrook retiring means the OKC jersey retirement conversation just moved to the front burner.

Jalen Williams: "dare I say Opening Night" for No. 0.

He'd join Nick Collison as only the 2nd number retired in franchise history.

#OKCThunder #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:00 AM ET

Russell Westbrook is retiring from the NBA, and let's take a moment to appreciate what we just witnessed.

209 career triple-doubles. Not 100. Not 150. Two hundred and nine. The next closest is Oscar Robertson with 181. Westbrook didn't just break the record — he lapped it.

Nine All-Star selections. The 2017 MVP season where he averaged a triple-double for an entire year — something most people said couldn't be done. He did it four times total.

Kevin Durant called his career "iconic" this week. Jalen Williams is already pushing for OKC to retire his No. 0 on Opening Night. He would be just the second number in franchise history to be retired, joining Nick Collison.

18 seasons. Relentless effort. A style of play that was entirely his own.

Whatever you thought of Russell Westbrook the player, you cannot argue with Russell Westbrook the competitor. He played every single game like it was his last.

Respect. 🏀

---

stories.title: Kawhi Leonard Investigation — ESPN/NBA War of Words — FOLLOW UP

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
ESPN says NBA found "no evidence" Ballmer paid Kawhi.

NBA fires back: report has "numerous and significant inaccuracies."

The investigators are now fighting each other. The Kawhi saga just got stranger.

#NBA

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
The Kawhi Leonard investigation has a resolution path: NBA-Clippers settlement talks have reportedly started.

Target: ~Sept 22 — one week before Toronto's Quebec City training camp.

Leonard and the Raptors are operating like the trade gets done.

#Raptors #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 11:00 AM ET

The Kawhi Leonard situation just took a wild new turn — and this time, it's not about Kawhi at all. It's about the media.

On August 17, ESPN published a bombshell report: the NBA had "found no evidence" that Steve Ballmer funneled money to Kawhi Leonard through the Aspiration and Daktronics sponsorship deals.

Within hours, the NBA hit back hard. Spokesman Mike Bass said the ESPN report "contains numerous and significant inaccuracies" — a rare and aggressive pushback from the league on a major outlet.

Here's where things stand:
✅ The investigation is narrowing to whether the Clippers improperly introduced Leonard to their business partners (a "failure to supervise" violation)
✅ NBA/Clippers settlement talks have reportedly started — which suggests both sides see a path out
✅ Kawhi Leonard has received zero indication his contract will be voided
✅ Leonard and the Raptors are still operating as if this trade completes

Target resolution: around September 22 — one week before Toronto training camp opens in Quebec City.

So even as ESPN and the NBA are fighting over what the investigation actually found, the destination hasn't changed: this trade appears to be completing. It's just taking the most dramatic possible route to get there.

---

stories.title: Wembanyama France vs. Serbia — Belgrade Preview — FOLLOW UP

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Wembanyama vs. Serbia in Belgrade tomorrow.

Wemby, Gobert, and Fournier for France.
Jokic's full Serbian squad on the other side.

Wemby: "I miss FIBA basketball."

This is must-watch summer hoops.

#NBA #FIBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:00 AM ET

Tomorrow night, Victor Wembanyama plays his first competitive basketball game since the 2024 Olympic final — and his opponent is a Serbian squad that includes Nikola Jokic.

France vs. Serbia. Belgrade. August 20.

This isn't a warmup. This is a legitimately marquee summer basketball matchup, and here's why: France is stacked. Wembanyama, Rudy Gobert, and Evan Fournier headline the roster. France went 5-1 in qualifying. New coach Frederic Fauthoux is working with Wemby for the first time.

On the other side? Serbia with Jokic — who just had another All-NBA season and is playing with something to prove heading into the 2026-27 NBA season.

Wembanyama said it himself: "I miss FIBA basketball." He chose this over resting through the summer. That tells you everything about how seriously he's taking it.

There's also a second game: August 23 in Orleans. But Belgrade tomorrow is the marquee.

Set your alarms.

---

stories.title: LaMelo Trade Details Confirmed — FOLLOW UP

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
The LaMelo Ball trade price, confirmed:

Minnesota gave: Naz Reid + 2033 unprotected 1st + 3 pick swaps + 3 second-rounders.

Anthony Edwards: "championship reality check."

LaMelo has never played a single playoff game. Stakes are enormous.

#Timberwolves #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 1:00 PM ET

The full price Minnesota paid to get LaMelo Ball is now confirmed — and it is steep.

The Timberwolves sent to Charlotte:
• Naz Reid
• 2033 unprotected first-round pick
• Three first-round pick swaps (2028, 2029, 2030)
• Three second-round picks (2029, 2032, 2033)

In return: LaMelo Ball and Josh Green.

Anthony Edwards wasted no time delivering a "championship reality check" after the deal — expectations in Minnesota are now elevated.

But here's the thing everyone keeps coming back to: LaMelo Ball has never played a single NBA playoff game. Not one. In his entire career.

That is the defining tension of this trade. If it works — if LaMelo's elite playmaking frees Edwards to score off the ball and Minnesota makes a deep playoff run — the price looks cheap. If LaMelo can't stay healthy or the chemistry is off, the Wolves gutted their depth for nothing.

The Ringer described it as "the Wolves betting the Anthony Edwards era" on this trade. That's exactly right.

Big bet. Big upside. Big risk.

---

stories.title: Stephen Curry Extension — 10 Days to Window — FOLLOW UP

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
10 days until Curry's extension window opens (Aug 29).

Max offer: 2yr/$136.7M.

Reports suggest Curry might prefer a shorter deal over the full max.

Either way — the most important Warriors date of the summer is 10 days away.

#Warriors #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:00 AM ET

Ten days.

That's how long Warriors fans have to wait until Stephen Curry is eligible to sign his extension — August 29 is the official window opener.

The max on the table: 2 years, $136.7 million.

But there are rumblings that Curry might not take the full max. Multiple reports suggest he's considering a shorter-term structure — giving him more flexibility in the years ahead. ESPN's Brian Windhorst called one potential approach "bold and risky."

What's not in question: mutual interest is real. Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. said he's "pretty confident" Curry will finish his career in Golden State. And Curry wants to stay — he just wants the team to show it can compete around him.

The Warriors lost the LeBron sweepstakes this offseason. That failure adds urgency to getting this done. A Curry who walks in 2027 as a first-time UFA would be the most stunning free agency story the league has seen in a decade.

Ten days.

---
